fields.problem: Warm pools hide cold-start latency by holding memory that sits idle most of the time, and snapshot restore, the memory-cheap alternative, is slow because the restored instance faults in its pages one at a time.
fields.stakes: Cold starts are frequent because most functions are invoked rarely; whoever can make snapshot restore fast removes the memory cost of warm pools for the whole long tail.
fields.thesis: The pages a function touches are stable across invocations and small relative to the snapshot, so reading that working set sequentially before the vCPU starts recovers most of a warm pool's latency at a fraction of its memory.

message.says: Serverless cold starts can be made fast from snapshots alone, without warm pools, by prefetching each function's recorded working set of pages before it resumes.
